title: What is a hat-trick? Three goals, one player
description: What is a hat-trick in football? Three goals belong to one player in one match. Discover why a brilliant personal score does not always mean victory.

sections.title: Three goals, one player
sections.html:
In football, also called soccer, a hat-trick means one player scores three goals in the same match. The team scoring three is not enough: those goals must belong to the same player.

Cambridge Dictionary defines the term through three scores in one game. It is a personal achievement inside a team sport.

sections.title: Give all three to Sam
sections.html:
Imagine Sam scores twice before half-time and once afterwards. That is a hat-trick. Spread Sam’s goals across three different matches, though, and the label no longer fits.

Now give Sam, Alex and Robin one goal each. The team still has three goals, but nobody has a hat-trick. Same scoreboard total; a very different story.

sections.title: A hat-trick can still end in defeat
sections.html:
Kylian Mbappé scored three times for France against Argentina in the 2022 World Cup final. FIFA’s record lists his hat-trick and the 3–3 final score.

Argentina then won the penalty shoot-out 4–2. Mbappé’s remarkable personal tally did not make France the winners. “Who scored three?” and “Who won?” can have different answers.

sections.title: Read the match, not just the total
sections.html:
Next time a headline announces a hat-trick, look for one player, three goals and one match. There is more information in that little phrase than in a bare team score.

For another football phrase worth knowing, try the offside rule. Or discover why a 90-minute game often lasts longer.
